speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our mission is to connect Singaporeans from doorstep to destination in Singapore and to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our aviation and maritime sectors are the lifeline of Singapore's economy.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They provide the global connectivity needed by companies and keep Singapore at the heart of international business and trade.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We face increasing competition from new hubs, market restructuring and alternative flight and shipping routes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We face strong headwinds, such as the heightened security environment and the global economic slowdown, which will also affect the growth of our airport and seaport and, hence, the livelihoods of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will support this shift by making it much easier to walk and cycle in Singapore, since this is how almost every public transport commuter gets to the MRT station or bus stop today.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With safe and comfortable facilities, we hope, too, that Singaporeans will increasingly walk or cycle to neighbourhood amenities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Technology and innovation, such as self-driving vehicles, the sharing economy and new urban designs, will also support a new mobility paradigm that does not revolve around the private car.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Indeed, a car-centric transport system is not sustainable in land-scarce Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Already, one million private vehicles ply the roads today and 12% of our land is used for roads.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: A growing number of cities are also decisively moving their transportation model away from private cars, for an improved urban environment and higher quality of life.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will further strengthen the competitiveness of our air and sea hubs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: To this end, we are undertaking major infrastructure projects.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In the longer term, the first set of berths of the new Tuas Terminal will be ready by 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Changi Airport Terminal 5 is expected to be completed in the second half of the 2020s while a three-runway system will be in place in the early 2020s.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, we will focus on innovative design and cutting-edge technology that maximises the efficiency and productivity of our air and sea ports.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our new infrastructure projects offer the best opportunities to do so, but we will also retrofit existing facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, we will deepen the services, capabilities and skills that anchor our competitiveness as a global aviation and maritime hub.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will continue to build up a comprehensive ecosystem of services and companies which make up Maritime Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will invest even more in air traffic management capabilities to remain top of the class, capable of providing the highest standards of safe and efficient air traffic services in our busy and complex airspace.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will continue to work with the industry, unions and educational institutions to train and develop Singaporeans so that they can seize the exciting and rewarding career opportunities in the aviation and maritime sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Page: 55 Our aspiration is for walking, cycling and riding public transport to become the way of life for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Improving rail reliability will continue to be our top priority.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA and the operators will be recruiting many additional engineers and technicians in order to further enhance maintenance capacity and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: It will be implementing more stringent maintenance requirements to better detect deficiencies upstream.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Major renewal works for the North-South and East-West Lines will be completed by 2018, which will further improve their reliability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In addition, the service levels of existing MRT lines and public buses will be raised further in the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Bus regularity and punctuality, for example, will see marked improvement under the bus contracting industry model.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At the same time, the expansion of our public transport capacity continues apace.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We are on track to double our rail network to 360 kilometres in the next 15 years, with a new line or MRT extension opening almost every year between now and 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: By then, there will be an MRT station within a five-minute walk from any location in the central area, and eight in 10 households will be within a 10-minute walk of a station by 2030.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Our transport network is also planned to enable the development of alternative business districts outside of the city centre, where jobs will be closer to homes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: New housing estates will be designed and existing estates retrofitted towards this "Walk, Cycle, Ride" aspiration.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Over the next five years, we will quadruple the length of covered walkways and build dedicated cycling paths in more towns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Ang Mo Kio and Tampines will pilot a fully integrated and seamless walking and cycling network.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Kampong Bugis will pilot new design concepts for private developments that facilitate seamless walking and cycling, while Bidadari Town will have a walking greenway and cycling paths connecting to its two MRT stations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We will build on these concepts for the town centres and our city centre as well, to create a more pleasant and safe walking experience for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Looking further ahead, self-driving vehicle technology will enable new concepts of mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We are planning and conducting trials and simulation studies to facilitate their future deployment, which will complement and radically improve the public transport experience, for example, in the first and last mile.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: With the support and partnership of Singaporeans, we hope to forge a society where people will give their cars a break and choose instead to "Walk, Cycle, Ride Singapore".
